lifecycle: CordisBoundNodeHost.drain -> NodeContainer.drain when measured in_flight is zero
CordisBoundNodeHost.dispose -> verify Rust state is draining or failed -> reverse Cordis Fiber disposal -> NodeContainer.dispose
mount failure -> NodeContainer.fail -> reverse Cordis Fiber disposal -> NodeContainer.dispose
graph_binding_rule: the actual mounted Cordis plugin plan entries must equal the immutable NodePluginPlan entries; graph_hash, manifest_hash, loaded_plan_hash and plan.hash must be the same verified hash before Rust declaration
in_flight_rule: Rust NodeContainer exclusively owns the atomic in-flight count; the JS host consumes typed status without storing a second counter; drain rejects when the Rust count is non-zero
transport_rule: the lifecycle port is a persistent line-delimited typed operation channel; the JS encoder exposes only declared lifecycle methods and the Rust decoder rejects every field outside that operation's schema; messages never carry business payload or metadata
forbidden: generic operation plus arbitrary fields encoder
unknown lifecycle request fields silently discarded
control/debug/error fields in provider or client business payload
required_tests: real Cordis mount drives Rust state to accepting
in-flight execution rejects drain and leaves state accepting
accepting-state disposal rejects before either lifecycle owner is mutated
Cordis graph/plan drift rejects before Rust declaration
Cordis mount failure drives Rust candidate through failed to disposed
Rust rejects metadata and business fields outside the selected lifecycle operation schema
JS rejects undeclared lifecycle fields before writing to the port
